review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the simp-tagged declarations (coe_embAt, projAt_embAt, projS_apply, transposeInv3Hom_apply). I compared them with the untagged companion lemmas and with how the proofs actually rewrite. I grepped the Definitions for transposeInv3 and transposeInvN lemmas and found no simp coverage there. Nothing was compiled, so I make no claim about observed simp behaviour. There were no loop risks or competing lemmas that I could justify. The two findings are about missing canonical lemmas and an inconsistent simp set. Both are low to moderate severity, because the file is a one-off solution file with few downstream users.

findings.declaration: KcRsCellRem.localAt_placeEmbed (together with the scoped simp lemmas coe_embAt, projAt_embAt, projS_apply)
findings.excerpt: theorem localAt_placeEmbed (x : GL (Fin 2) (p.adicCompletion ℚ)) : localAt ℚ p (placeEmbed ℚ p x) = x := by
findings.problem: The scoped simp set is cut off one step before its normal form. coe_embAt rewrites `(embAt p x : AdelicGL2 ..)` to `placeEmbed ℚ p x`, and projS_apply rewrites `projS SQ g p` to `localAt ℚ p ↑g`. The lemma that finishes the reduction, `localAt_placeEmbed`, is not simp. It is a clean, unconditional rewrite, and `projAt_embAt` is already simp and is proved from it. As a result `projS_embS` (lines 390-401) cannot use simp. It does `rw [projS_apply, coe_embAt]` and later `rw [localAt_placeEmbed, ...]` by hand. The simp set therefore leaves `localAt ℚ p (placeEmbed ℚ p x)` as a stuck term that no simp lemma reduces.
findings.proposed_change: Tag `localAt_placeEmbed` with `@[scoped simp]`, like its neighbours `coe_embAt` and `projAt_embAt`. Optionally also tag `localAt_placeEmbed_of_ne`, which has a hypothesis `q ≠ p` that simp can discharge when it is given. Then the same-place branch of `projS_embS` reduces to `simp [projS_apply, coe_embAt]` plus the `Pi.mulSingle` lemmas.
findings.benefit: The simp set that already exists (coe_embAt, projS_apply) now computes local components of embedded elements to the end, so callers no longer have to name the finishing lemma. The tagged `projAt_embAt` and its untagged proof lemma also become consistent.

findings.excerpt: @[scoped simp] theorem transposeInv3Hom_apply (g : GL (Fin 3) A) : transposeInv3Hom g = transposeInv3 g := rfl
findings.problem: The only simp lemma in the transposeInv3 block, `transposeInv3Hom_apply`, unfolds a bundled hom. `transposeInv3Hom` is never used in the file. The algebraic lemmas that are used, `transposeInv3_mul`, `transposeInv3_one`, `transposeInv3_inv` and `transposeInv3_transposeInv3`, are not simp. Every use is an explicit rewrite chain, for example `rw [hloc, kkAt, map_mul, map_mul, transposeInv3_mul, transposeInv3_mul]` in `isolation_identity`. A plain `simp` therefore cannot push `transposeInv3` through products, inverses or the identity. The same holds for the Definitions-side `transposeInvN_mul`, which the file also rewrites manually. The interface has a dead normalisation lemma and no usable ones.
findings.proposed_change: Tag the plain lemmas `transposeInv3_mul`, `transposeInv3_one`, `transposeInv3_inv` and `transposeInv3_transposeInv3` with `@[simp]` (or `@[scoped simp]`). Drop `transposeInv3Hom_apply` as simp, or drop the unused Hom. Termination is fine: `mul`, `one` and `inv` push the function inward, and the involution lemma strictly shrinks the term. Keep `transposeInv3_map` out of simp unless its direction is chosen deliberately.
findings.benefit: The multi-step `rw` chains around `transposeInv3 (iotaGL (unipotent x * u * y))` can be replaced by a single `simp only [map_mul, transposeInv3_mul]`. The unused hom-unfolding simp lemma no longer suggests a canonical form that nothing uses.
